algorithm.info.title: Algorithm information
algorithm.info.description.aes: AES is a symmetric block cipher with a 128-bit block size. The selected mode determines authentication, padding requirements and streaming capabilities.
algorithm.info.description.ascon: Ascon-128 (AEAD) is a permutation-based authenticated encryption algorithm standardized in NIST SP 800-232.
algorithm.info.description.serpent: Serpent is a symmetric 128-bit block cipher. In this application it is combined with CBC and HMAC-SHA256 using an Encrypt-then-MAC construction.
algorithm.info.description.camellia: Camellia is a symmetric 128-bit block cipher supporting 128, 192 and 256-bit keys.
algorithm.info.description.3des: 3DES is a legacy symmetric block cipher with a 64-bit block size. It is retained mainly for compatibility and educational comparison.
algorithm.info.description.chacha: ChaCha20-Poly1305 combines the ChaCha20 stream cipher with Poly1305 authentication to provide authenticated encryption.
algorithm.info.description.xchacha: XChaCha20-Poly1305 extends ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a 192-bit nonce, making random nonce generation safer for file encryption.
algorithm.info.description.salsa20: Salsa20 is a symmetric stream cipher. It provides confidentiality but does not provide authentication by itself.
algorithm.info.description.threefish: Threefish-Skein-MAC combines the Threefish tweakable block cipher in a counter-based streaming construction with keyed Skein authentication using Encrypt-then-MAC.
algorithm.info.description.rsa.pss: RSA-PSS is an asymmetric digital signature scheme based on RSA.
algorithm.info.description.rsa.oaep: RSA-OAEP uses RSA to protect a randomly generated AES-256 key, while AES-GCM provides authenticated streaming encryption of the file.
algorithm.info.description.eddsa: EdDSA digital signatures using streaming prehash variants. Ed25519ph uses SHA-512 and Ed448ph uses SHAKE256.
algorithm.info.description.ecdsa: ECDSA creates digital signatures using NIST elliptic curves and SHA-2 or SHA-3 hash functions. Files are hashed incrementally for streaming operation.
algorithm.info.description.ml.kem: ML-KEM is a NIST-standardized post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism based on module lattices. In this application, it establishes a shared secret that is used to derive an AES-256-GCM key for streaming file encryption.
algorithm.info.description.ml.dsa: ML-DSA is a NIST-standardized post-quantum digital signature algorithm based on module lattices. It provides authentication and integrity verification against both classical and quantum-capable adversaries.
algorithm.info.description.slh.dsa: SLH-DSA is a NIST-standardized stateless hash-based post-quantum digital signature algorithm. Its security relies primarily on the properties of cryptographic hash functions.
algorithm.info.mode.gcm: Authenticated encryption using counter mode and GHASH authentication.
algorithm.info.mode.eax: Authenticated encryption combining CTR encryption with authentication.
algorithm.info.mode.siv: Misuse-resistant authenticated encryption using a synthetic initialization vector.
algorithm.info.mode.ccm: Authenticated encryption combining CTR mode with CBC-MAC.
algorithm.info.mode.ocb: Authenticated encryption designed for low overhead and high performance.
algorithm.info.mode.ctr: Counter mode converts a block cipher into a stream-like construction. It does not provide authentication.
algorithm.info.mode.cbc: Cipher Block Chaining links each plaintext block with the previous ciphertext block. It does not provide authentication by itself.
algorithm.info.mode.ecb: Each block is encrypted independently. Identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks.
algorithm.info.mode.cfb: Cipher Feedback converts a block cipher into a self-synchronizing stream-like mode.
algorithm.info.mode.ofb: Output Feedback converts a block cipher into a synchronous stream-like mode.
algorithm.info.mode.ascon.128.aead: Authenticated encryption defined by NIST SP 800-232 using a 128-bit key, nonce and authentication tag.
algorithm.info.mode.serpent.cbc.hmac: Serpent-CBC with PKCS#7 padding and HMAC-SHA256 authentication using an Encrypt-then-MAC construction.
